# Cinematic Vocabulary Runtime Discovery

The Awtsmoos gives cinema more than one named angle or one named dissolve; Awtsmoos.com keeps those names lawful so AI intent, canonical validation, adapter preservation, and renderer fallback can agree in one living tongue.

## Direct runtime evidence
- The native ffmpeg proof page failed before session creation because the canonical compiler rejected authored `two-shot`, `light-wipe`, and `particle-dissolve` values.
- The three-minute intent intentionally authors these values in `ActTwoScenes.js` and `ActThreeScenes.js`; they are not accidental strings injected by the proof page.
- `MovieIntentNormalizer.normalizeCamera()` preserves a camera `size` as its canonical `kind` unless an angle creates a stronger normalization such as high-angle, low-angle, or overhead.
- Therefore `two-shot` with `eye-level` intentionally survives into canonical camera semantics.
- `MovieIntentNormalizer.normalizeTransition()` intentionally maps `transition.type` directly to canonical `transition.kind`, preserving `light-wipe` and `particle-dissolve`.
- `CanvasMovieRenderer` safely renders every transition kind through a generic edge treatment and specializes only `flash`; adding richer semantic kinds cannot break its basic fallback rendering.
- `CanvasWorldPainter` uses camera kind for horizon heuristics and safely falls back to the ordinary horizon ratio for un-specialized framings such as `two-shot`.

## Decision
Promote `two-shot`, `light-wipe`, and `particle-dissolve` into the canonical semantic vocabulary. Do not flatten them to `medium`, `wipe`, or `crossfade`, because doing so would erase authored intent that adapters and future renderers can preserve even when the current Canvas proof renderer degrades gracefully.

## Additional proof-truth repair
The ffmpeg proof HTML promises 640×360 at 12fps, while the three-minute intent defaults to 1280×720 at 24fps. The proof controller must explicitly pass `width: 640`, `height: 360`, and `fps: 12` so runtime evidence matches its visible contract and the acceptance target remains 2,160 frames for 180 seconds.

Hash-gate and rewrite `MovieSemanticKinds.js` plus the dedicated ffmpeg proof controller; add a new cinematic-vocabulary regression test; run the complete test gate; cold-reload the 30-second ffmpeg proof.
